title: Report Writing
summary: A report is a factual account of an event, topic or issue, written so that someone unfamiliar with it learns everything needed. It may contain facts, figures, analysis, opinions, suggestions, recommendations, maps, graphs and tables. Firms and government offices use reports to communicate information objectively; students write them as assignments.

Reports are written on your own initiative, in reply to a letter, at regular intervals, or to record an incident. They must be comprehensive but brief, factual, logically arranged and formal — usually in the third person, often in the passive voice and in simple language.
Process: collect ideas → organise → draft (right medium, audience, tone, bias-free language) → edit → rewrite → submit. How a report is written depends on who will read it and why.
## Published reports — school magazine, newsletter, newspaper

Headline (catchy, brief), byline ('By …'), lead paragraph answering who, what, when, where and why, second paragraph with more details in order, third paragraph with eyewitness accounts or quotations, concluding paragraph with future action. Newspaper reports follow the inverted pyramid — most important facts first — and are in the past tense.
School magazine/newsletter reports give in-depth information for a specific readership; newspapers give brief, factual news to the general public.

Format: (letterhead), To (recipient and designation), From (writer and designation), date, subject, opening statement, findings/observations (often numbered), advantages and disadvantages or causes, recommendations, conclusion, signature and name.
Do's: be objective, give evidence, use valid arguments. Don'ts: let personal feelings interfere, rely on one piece of evidence, generalise or jump to conclusions.
Types: external, internal, routine, special, financial, review, oral, long (formal) and short (informal) reports.

sa2: A report is a precise, factual account of an event, topic or issue, presented logically so that the reader can understand it and make decisions.
How should you structure the lead paragraph of a newspaper report?
Put the most important information first, answering who, what, when, where and why (and how) in a few sentences.
What is the role of quotations in a report?
Quotations from eyewitnesses or officials add authenticity and human interest, and show the views of people involved.
What points need to be kept in mind while writing an accident report?

Give the date, time and place; describe what happened in order; mention the people and vehicles involved, injuries and damage; include eyewitness accounts; and state the action taken — factually and objectively.
la4: A School Annual Day Celebration was organised by your school on 25th November, 2025. Write a news clipping for the Residents' Welfare Association about the event.

ANNUAL DAY CELEBRATED WITH ZEST
By Kavya Rao, Green Park

Sunrise Public School celebrated its Annual Day on 25 November 2025 in the school auditorium. Mr S. Iyer, District Education Officer, was the chief guest.
The programme opened with the lighting of the lamp and a welcome song. Students presented a folk-dance medley, a skit on cleanliness and an orchestra recital. The Principal read the annual report, and prizes were given for academics, sports and community service.
"Our children have shown that talent grows where it is nurtured," said the chief guest. Parents praised the discipline and creativity on display.
The event ended with the National Anthem. The school plans to open its new library to residents next month.

As Purchase Officer for Neva Silk Manufacturers, Ambikapur, you wish to change the vendor who supplies textile raw material. Submit a report to the Managing Director listing why the new vendor would be better.

Neva Silk Manufacturers, Ambikapur
To: The Managing Director
From: Purchase Officer
Date: 5 January 2026
Subject: Proposal to change the supplier of raw silk

As desired, I compared our present supplier with Shakti Yarns, Raipur. My findings:
1. Quality: Shakti's yarn has fewer defects (2% against 7%).
2. Price: 8% cheaper, with a further 3% discount on bulk orders.
3. Delivery: within 5 days against our present 15 days; nearer location cuts freight.
4. Credit: 45 days' credit against 30.
Disadvantage: a new vendor is untried; this can be met by a three-month trial order.
Recommendation: place a trial order with Shakti Yarns and review after three months.
Sd/-
Purchase Officer
A Yoga Shivir was organised by your colony on 21st June, International Day of Yoga. Write a news clipping for the Residents' Welfare Association in about 120 words.

YOGA SHIVIR DRAWS HUNDREDS
By Rohan Mehra, Shanti Vihar

On International Day of Yoga, 21 June, the Shanti Vihar RWA organised a Yoga Shivir in the community park from 6 to 8 a.m. Over 250 residents of all ages took part.
Yoga teacher Ms Anjali Sen led sessions on surya namaskar, pranayama and meditation, and explained how daily practice reduces stress and lifestyle diseases. Senior citizens were given simple chair exercises.
"I feel fresh and energetic," said 72-year-old Mr Gupta. Children enjoyed a special session of animal poses.
The RWA has decided to hold free yoga classes every Sunday morning.
You visited Jeny Residency, Pune. Write a report on its facilities to the General Manager, P & G, Mumbai.

To: The General Manager, P & G, Mumbai
From: Administrative Officer
Date: 8 March 2026
Subject: Report on facilities at Jeny Residency, Pune

As instructed, I visited Jeny Residency on 6 March to assess it for our training programme.
Findings:
1. Conference hall seating 150, with projector and sound system.
2. A large open lawn suitable for group activities.
3. Forty clean, spacious rooms, sufficient for our participants.
4. A quiet, green campus away from city noise.
Drawback: it is 20 km from the station; the hotel provides a shuttle on request.
Recommendation: the venue is suitable and may be booked for April.
Sd/-
Administrative Officer
Prepare a report on a fire incident in the staff room of your office caused by an overheated microwave. Include date, time, location, cause, damage and action taken.

To: The Administrative Head
From: Safety Officer
Date: 15 February 2026
Subject: Fire in the staff room on 14 February 2026

1. Incident: At about 1.15 p.m. on 14 February a fire broke out in the second-floor staff room.
2. Cause: an overheated microwave oven with a faulty cord.
3. Action: staff used the fire extinguisher, the building was evacuated and the fire brigade arrived at 1.30 p.m. No one was injured.
4. Damage: the microwave, a cupboard and some files were burnt.
Recommendations: check all appliances monthly, replace old wiring, conduct fire drills and train staff to use extinguishers.
Sd/-
Safety Officer
As Office Manager of Ravi Industries, New Delhi, you inspected buildings for shifting the office. Write a report to the Managing Director recommending one.

Ravi Industries, 16 Pragati Tower, Nehru Place, New Delhi
To: Mr S. K. Singh, Managing Director
From: C. Rao, Office Manager
Date: 7 May 2026
Subject: Suitable premises for the office

As desired, I inspected several buildings in South Delhi and recommend Jain Building, Kailash Colony.
1. Two storeys with 15 large, well-lit, airy rooms; partitions possible.
2. Adequate toilets for men and women; watchmen's quarters near the gate.
3. Bus stop 200 yards and metro station 500 yards away.
Disadvantage: limited parking; junior staff can use public transport.
Action: preliminary talks with the owner, Mr Anupam Jain, have begun; alterations will cost about Rs 40,000.
The Directors may inspect the building before deciding.
Sd/-
C. Rao
